name: Amber Eau de Parfum
summary: A warm, quiet amber that settles close to skin instead of filling the room. It is an easy entry point if you want softness without powder or dessert-like sweetness.
sampleAdvice: A strong value match, but test it on skin if musks sometimes disappear on you.

name: You
summary: Peppery at first, then softly powdery and musky. You suits someone who wants a recognisable signature scent that still feels casual enough for a weekday.
sampleAdvice: Try it for a full afternoon. Ambrox-heavy scents can feel very different from one wearer to another.

name: Not a Perfume
summary: A deliberately spare, woody amber scent built around Cetalox. Choose it when most traditional perfumes feel too busy, floral or sweet.
sampleAdvice: Some people become nose-blind to this style quickly, so ask someone else whether they can still smell it before overspraying.

name: Goddess
summary: Creamy vanilla made airier by lavender. It is polished and warmly noticeable, with more structure than a bakery-style gourmand.
sampleAdvice: The vanilla develops over time. Judge it after the dry-down, especially if you are sensitive to sweetness.

name: Fleur de Peau
summary: A tactile iris-musk with a soft, cosmetic powderiness. It feels intimate but composed, especially if you want a skin scent with more depth and persistence.
sampleAdvice: Sample first if powder is usually difficult for you. This is elegant, but the powdery texture is central rather than incidental.

name: Bal d'Afrique
summary: Bright citrus and marigold over a soft woody base. It reads joyful and dressed-up without becoming sugary, which makes it unusually flexible for a statement fragrance.
sampleAdvice: Check the late dry-down on your skin. The opening is brighter than the musky, woody finish.

name: Myth
summary: A clean floral musk with enough white cedar to keep it from feeling shampoo-like. It works well when you want refinement without a strong perfume trail.
sampleAdvice: A sensible office option. Test the travel size first if longevity matters more to you than softness.

name: No.04 Bois de Balincourt
summary: Creamy sandalwood sharpened with cedar, vetiver and spice. It gives a room-temperature warmth rather than a sugary one, and wears easily across seasons.
sampleAdvice: A good bridge between woody and warm scents. Sample if sandalwood fragrances sometimes turn pickle-like on your skin.

name: I Don't Know What
summary: A radiant fragrance framework that can be worn alone or over another scent. It is the most interesting match here for someone who wants projection, layering and modern woody transparency.
sampleAdvice: Treat it as both a perfume and a styling tool. Test it alone before deciding what to layer beneath it.

name: Milk
summary: A very quiet bergamot, white musk and amber blend designed to sit close and layer easily. Pick it when you want comfort and flexibility more than a dramatic entrance.
sampleAdvice: The lightness is intentional. Choose it for intimacy, not for room-filling projection.

name: Donna Born In Roma Eau de Parfum
summary: An eau de parfum combining floral and amber and spice, built around Jasmine Sambac, Cashmeran and Bourbon Vanilla. It suits a balanced scent brief and is best treated as a skin test, not a blind buy.
sampleAdvice: Give the floral heart at least an hour on skin, especially if powder or white flowers can become dominant for you.
